scenes.eyebrow: Crypto crash explained · as of 21 Nov 2026
scenes.headline: Bitcoin is down about half from its high
scenes.voiceover: If you're searching crypto crash, here's where things stand. In October twenty twenty-five, Bitcoin hit about one hundred and twenty-six thousand dollars. In mid-November twenty twenty-six, it's trading at roughly half of that. Is that normal? Bitcoin has fallen further before. These are its seven worst crashes, ranked by one simple rule.

scenes.headline: How far Bitcoin fell from a peak to its next low
scenes.body: Days or months, each fall counted once. Education, not financial advice. No predictions.
scenes.voiceover: The rule: how far Bitcoin's price fell from a peak to its next low, whether that took two days or a whole year. And each fall is counted only once. This is education, not financial advice, and we won't be making any predictions.

scenes.headline: Black Thursday
scenes.voiceover: Number seven.

scenes.headline: A pandemic panic, and half the price gone in two days
scenes.voiceover: Black Thursday, March twenty twenty. As COVID-19 shut the world down, investors sold almost everything. Bitcoin went from around eight thousand dollars to under four thousand, losing about half its value in two days.

scenes.name: Black Thursday
scenes.headline: Borrowed money made it worse
scenes.voiceover: What made it so fast? Many traders were using borrowed money. When prices fell, exchanges automatically sold their positions, and those forced sales pushed prices down even further.

scenes.headline: China crackdown + Tesla U-turn
scenes.voiceover: Number six.

scenes.headline: A record high, then a one-two punch
scenes.voiceover: May twenty twenty-one. Bitcoin had just hit a record of around sixty-four thousand dollars. Then Tesla stopped accepting Bitcoin, citing energy concerns, and China cracked down on Bitcoin mining.

scenes.name: China crackdown + Tesla U-turn
scenes.headline: Nearly $1 trillion gone in a week
scenes.voiceover: Bitcoin fell fifty-three percent. Across the whole crypto market, nearly one trillion dollars in value disappeared in a single week.

scenes.headline: The 2025–26 crash
scenes.voiceover: Number five.

scenes.headline: The crash we're living through
scenes.voiceover: This is the one many of you are living through right now. In October twenty twenty-five, Bitcoin hit a record of about one hundred and twenty-six thousand dollars. On the tenth of October, after a US threat of one hundred percent tariffs on China, about nineteen billion dollars in borrowed trading bets were wiped out in a single day, the largest liquidation on record.

scenes.name: The 2025–26 crash
scenes.headline: Biggest in dollars, but not in percent
scenes.receipt: Bloomberg; CoinGlass; CryptoTicker (CoinGecko data) · as of 21 Nov 2026
scenes.voiceover: By February, Bitcoin had fallen to about sixty thousand dollars, and in July twenty twenty-six it touched fifty-eight thousand five hundred. That's a fall of about fifty-three and a half percent so far. Bitcoin Magazine calls it the largest dollar drop in Bitcoin's history. But in percentage terms, Bitcoin has fallen further before. This crash isn't over, so this number could still change.

scenes.headline: The 2022 collapse
scenes.voiceover: Number four.

scenes.headline: Terra, Celsius, FTX: one chain breaking
scenes.voiceover: twenty twenty-two. In May, a so-called stablecoin, UST, that was meant to stay at one dollar fell to just twelve cents, and its partner coin LUNA collapsed with it. An estimated forty billion dollars was wiped out. Next, the crypto lenders Celsius and Three Arrows Capital failed.

scenes.name: The 2022 collapse
scenes.headline: Then FTX: an $8 billion hole
scenes.voiceover: Then, in November, the exchange FTX collapsed, with an eight billion dollar hole in its accounts. Customer money had allegedly been moved to a sister trading firm. From its peak, Bitcoin fell seventy-seven percent.

scenes.headline: Crypto winter
scenes.voiceover: Number three.

scenes.headline: The ICO bubble bursts
scenes.voiceover: the crypto winter of twenty eighteen. In late twenty seventeen, Bitcoin reached about nineteen thousand seven hundred dollars, in a frenzy of new coins being sold to the public, called I C Os.

scenes.name: Crypto winter
scenes.headline: A whole year of falling
scenes.voiceover: Then the bubble burst. Over the following year, Bitcoin lost eighty-four percent of its value. It took about two years to reach a new high.

scenes.headline: China ban + Mt. Gox
scenes.voiceover: Number two.

scenes.headline: A ban, then the biggest exchange goes dark
scenes.voiceover: twenty thirteen to twenty fifteen. In December twenty thirteen, China's central bank barred banks from handling Bitcoin, and its price halved in about two days, from over twelve hundred dollars to under six hundred.

scenes.name: China ban + Mt. Gox
scenes.headline: 850,000 bitcoins: gone
scenes.voiceover: Then, in February twenty fourteen, Mt. Gox, the exchange that once handled most Bitcoin trading, froze withdrawals. It later revealed that about eight hundred and fifty thousand bitcoins had been lost. Bitcoin's fall reached eighty-five percent.

scenes.headline: The 2011 crash
scenes.voiceover: Number one.

scenes.headline: From $32 to one cent
scenes.voiceover: twenty eleven, when Bitcoin was barely two years old. In June, a hacker broke into Mt. Gox, which handled about ninety percent of all Bitcoin trading, and sold stolen coins at any price. On that one exchange, Bitcoin's price crashed from about thirty-two dollars to one cent.

scenes.name: The 2011 crash
scenes.headline: The worst fall in Bitcoin's history
scenes.voiceover: The one-cent price only happened on that one exchange. But over the whole of twenty eleven, Bitcoin lost ninety-four percent of its value. By this rule, it's the worst crash in Bitcoin's history.

scenes.eyebrow: Bitcoin's fall, peak to low (%) · *still open, as of 21 Nov 2026
scenes.headline: Seven crashes, one rule
scenes.voiceover: Here they are side by side. The crash happening now is the biggest ever in dollars, but by percentage, four earlier crashes were deeper.

scenes.headline: A promise of fixed value
scenes.voiceover: So what can we learn, without predicting anything? Red flag one: a promise that something can't lose value. UST was meant to stay at one dollar. It fell to twelve cents.

scenes.headline: Not knowing who holds your coins
scenes.voiceover: Red flag two: not knowing who actually holds your coins. When Mt. Gox and FTX failed, people who kept coins there were stuck.

scenes.headline: Frozen withdrawals. Borrowed money.
scenes.receipt: Mt. Gox froze withdrawals (Feb 2014); CoinGlass ($19bn liquidated, 10 Oct 2025)
scenes.voiceover: Red flag three: withdrawals being frozen. That's how the Mt. Gox collapse began. And red flag four: borrowed money. On the tenth of October twenty twenty-five, about nineteen billion dollars of borrowed bets were wiped out in a day.

scenes.headline: History, not a forecast
scenes.voiceover: And is Bitcoin history repeating? Three earlier cycles each saw Bitcoin fall roughly eighty percent before reaching new highs. That's history, not a forecast. Nobody knows what happens next, and anyone who says they do is guessing.
